definition: P32 ward-level evidence-state closures for the 12 KIHBS/Kenya Housing Survey, 2021 Kenya Time Use Survey, 2019 KPHC analytical-report (Disability, Labour Force), 2022 KDHS and Kenya Poverty Report 2022 (KCHS) indicators, extending each indicator's already-verified P31 constituency-level closure (data/completeness/evidence-states.json, contract_id prefixes P31-KHS-CONSTITUENCY-CLOSURE, P31-TUS-CONSTITUENCY-CLOSURE, P31-KPHC-ANALYTICAL-CONSTITUENCY-CLOSURE, P31-KDHS-CONSTITUENCY-CLOSURE, P31-KCHS-POVERTY-CONSTITUENCY-CLOSURE) down to all 1,450 wards. A ward is strictly finer than a constituency, so a household-survey or census-tabulation domain of estimation that was already verified not to reach the 290 constituencies certainly does not reach the 1,450 wards; each entry restates the verified constituency-level citation in full and explains why it applies a fortiori at ward level, and none manufactures a zero, proxy, regional inheritance or spatially-allocated observation. This file is consumed only by scripts/p29/build-local-54-slot-ledger.mjs (via its supplementaryEvidenceFiles list), exactly like data/completeness/evidence-states.json, kept separate to avoid merge contention with other P32 batches editing the shared evidence-states.json file concurrently.

states.period_label: 2023/24 Kenya Housing Survey · constituency disaggregation not designed (county is the finest domain of estimation) -- extended a fortiori to ward level (P32)
states.source: KNBS 2023/24 Kenya Housing Survey Basic Report, Chapter 2 (Sections 2.1 Survey Design, 2.3 Sample size determination, 2.4 Sampling frame)
states.reason: EXTENDS the already-verified P31 constituency-level closure P31-KHS-CONSTITUENCY-CLOSURE-2026-09-18 (indicator_code IND-COMPUTER-USE, status governed_unavailable) to ward level. That closure found, and this ward-level entry re-affirms verbatim: "The 2023/24 Kenya Housing Survey's own Chapter 2 methodology (Section 2.1 'Survey Design', Basic Report p.10) states the survey was designed for 'estimating housing indicators at national, rural, urban and county levels' -- county, not constituency, is the explicit design domain. Section 2.3 'Sample size determination' confirms the household sample (25,900 households, 1,295 clusters) was 'computed independently for each county' using a formula with a county-specific design effect and relative-standard-error target, i.e. precision was engineered for 47 county estimates, not 290 constituency estimates (~6x finer). Section 2.4 'Sampling frame' confirms the 47 counties were stratified into only 92 sampling strata (one urban and one rural stratum per county, purely urban for Nairobi City and Mombasa) with clusters selected within those strata -- there is no constituency-level stratum, allocation or precision target anywhere in the design. Deriving a constituency figure from this survey would require either treating unweighted intra-county cluster counts (which the survey's own Section 2.8 weighting scheme exists specifically to correct for non-proportional allocation) as a designed constituency estimate, or spatially allocating the published county rate downward -- both are prohibited by this Atlas's anti-fabrication rule and by the survey_small_area treatment class's own condition to 'respect survey design/domain and sampling uncertainty' and 'never copy parent survey rates downward' (data/policy/local-54-indicator-contract.json)." A ward is strictly finer than a constituency -- Kenya's 1,450 wards are a strict subdivision of its 290 constituencies (every constituency contains multiple wards), so a domain-of-estimation ceiling that already stops at the county level (47 units) relative to 290 constituencies applies with even greater force relative to 1,450 wards, which are on average roughly 5x finer than constituencies and roughly 31x finer than counties. Nothing in the underlying source's design changes between the constituency and ward level: the same sampling strata (or, for the 2019 KPHC analytical reports, the same published tabulation domains), and the same absence of any sub-county allocation or precision target, apply unchanged. A fresh sanity check on 2026-09-19 (re-searching KNBS publication pages and the underlying report itself for any newer edition, addendum or small-area-estimation product) found no evidence that this survey/census design, or any successor publication of it, has added a constituency- or ward-level domain of estimation since the P31 closure was verified on 2026-09-18. Per this Atlas's anti-fabrication rule and the survey_small_area / census-tabulation treatment class conditions in data/policy/local-54-indicator-contract.json, the published county (or, where applicable, county/residence) value is never spatially allocated or copied downward to manufacture a ward figure.
states.evidence_constraint: survey_small_area treatment class: county is the documented finest domain of estimation (or, for the two 2019 KPHC analytical reports, the finest theme actually tabulated and published) for the underlying source; no constituency-level series exists and none may be derived by spatial allocation of the published county value. No ward-level series exists either, a fortiori: the same finest-domain ceiling that rules out the 290 constituencies rules out the 1,450 (strictly finer) wards, and none may be derived by spatial allocation of the published county value down to any ward.

states.period_label: 2019 KPHC Analytical Report on Disability · no sub-county table published for this theme -- extended a fortiori to ward level (P32)
states.source: KNBS 2019 KPHC Analytical Report on Disability, List of Tables (pp. iv-v) and Table 2.13 (p.35)
states.reason: EXTENDS the already-verified P31 constituency-level closure P31-KPHC-ANALYTICAL-CONSTITUENCY-CLOSURE-2026-09-18 (indicator_code IND-DISABILITY-PREVALENCE, status governed_unavailable) to ward level. That closure found, and this ward-level entry re-affirms verbatim: "Unlike the 2019 KPHC's basic population-count volumes (Volumes I-IV), which tabulate raw enumeration counts down to sub-location, the Analytical Report on Disability is a cross-tabulation report profiling one census theme (disability status/domain/severity) against demographic and socioeconomic characteristics, with its own independently-scoped table plan. Its own 'List of Tables' (report pp. iv-v) was downloaded and inspected directly: across all ~36 numbered tables (Tables 1.1 through 5.3) and 28 lettered appendices, every geographic breakdown used is 'County' and/or 'Residence' (urban/rural) -- e.g. Table 2.10 'Distribution of PWDs by County' (p.31), Table 2.13 'Disability Prevalence by County and Residence' (p.35 -- the table this indicator's county-level observations are drawn from), Table 2.16 'Percentage Distribution of PWDs by Number of Disabilities, Sex and Counties' (p.43), and Appendices 1-4 and 22-25 (all 'by ...
